nodes.name: secondary pulmonary lobule
nodes.definition:
Anatomy.—The lobule is the smallest unit of lung surrounded by connective-tissue septa, as defined by Miller (78) and Heitzman et al (40). The lobule is also referred to as the secondary pulmonary lobule; it contains a variable number of acini, is irregularly polyhedral in shape, and varies in size from 1.0 to 2.5 cm in diameter. The centrilobular structures, or core structures, include bronchioles and their accompanying pulmonary arterioles and lymphatic vessels. The connective-tissue septa surrounding the pulmonary lobule—the interlobular septa, which contain veins and lymphatic vessels—are best developed in the periphery in the anterior, lateral, and juxtamediastinal regions of the upper and middle lobes. 
CT scans.—On thin-section CT scans, the three basic components of the lobule—the interlobular septa and septal structures, the central lobular region (centrilobular structures), and the lobular parenchyma—can be identified, particularly in disease states. Peripheral lobules are more uniform in appearance and pyramidal in shape than are central lobules (4) (Fig 35).  [Fleischner Society]

nodes.name: early subacute

nodes.name: late subacute
nodes.definition: Roughly one to four weeks. Extracellular methaemoglobin.

nodes.name: chronic
nodes.definition: Beyond a month. Haemosiderin and ferritin.

nodes.name: indeterminate age
nodes.definition: The appearance does not permit dating.

nodes.definition: Ordered flow, uniform colour.

nodes.name: turbulent
nodes.definition: Disordered flow, visible swirling and colour mixing distal to the narrowing.

nodes.definition: Under 50 percent. Velocity stays low and steady through the segment.

nodes.name: significant
nodes.definition: 50 percent or more. Velocity surges through the narrowed gap, usually with turbulence distal to it.

nodes.name: compressive
nodes.definition: Adjacent space-occupying process compressing the lung.

nodes.name: obstructive
nodes.definition: Resorption of gas distal to an obstructed airway. Implies an obstructing lesion.

nodes.name: cicatricial

nodes.definition: The data presented do not permit categorization as present or absent.

nodes.name: unknown

nodes.definition: The density characteristics of a pulmonary nodule on CT.

nodes.name: solid
nodes.definition: The nodule completely obscures the underlying lung parenchyma.

nodes.name: part-solid
nodes.definition: The nodule contains both a solid component and a ground-glass component.

nodes.name: non-solid
nodes.definition: The nodule does not obscure the underlying lung parenchyma. Pure ground-glass.

nodes.name: calcification

nodes.name: none
nodes.definition: No calcification is identified.

nodes.name: central
nodes.definition: Calcification occupies the centre of the lesion.

nodes.name: popcorn
nodes.definition: Coarse, clustered, chondroid calcification.

nodes.name: punctate
nodes.definition: Small discrete foci of calcification.

nodes.name: coarse
nodes.definition: Dense, chunky calcification without a specific pattern.

nodes.name: peripheral / rim
nodes.definition: Calcification at the margin of the lesion.

nodes.name: echogenicity
nodes.definition: The reflectivity of the lesion relative to the adjacent parenchyma on ultrasound.

nodes.definition: No internal echoes.

nodes.name: very hypoechoic
nodes.definition: Markedly less echogenic than adjacent strap muscle.
nodes.source_definition: [TI-RADS]: Decreased echogenicity relative to adjacent neck musculature

nodes.name: hypoechoic
nodes.definition: Less echogenic than the adjacent parenchyma.

[TI-RADS}: Decreased echogenicity relative to thyroid tissue.  [LI-RADS] Echogenicity less than background liver.

nodes.name: isoechoic
nodes.definition: Equal in echogenicity to the adjacent parenchyma.

nodes.name: hyperechoic
nodes.definition: More echogenic than the adjacent parenchyma.
nodes.source_definition: BI-RADS US:  having increased echogenicity relative to fat or equal to fibroglandular tissue.  [TI-RADS]: Increased echogenicity relative to thyroid tissue [LI-RADS] Echogenicity more than background liver.

nodes.name: mixed cystic and solid

nodes.name: homogeneous
nodes.definition: Uniform uptake throughout.

nodes.name: heterogeneous
nodes.definition: Non-uniform uptake.

nodes.name: peripheral nodular discontinuous

nodes.name: arterial hyperenhancement with washout
nodes.definition: Uptake exceeding parenchyma in the arterial phase with subsequent relative hypoenhancement.

nodes.name: wall character
nodes.definition: The thickness and regularity of the wall bounding a fluid-filled structure.

nodes.name: imperceptible
nodes.definition: No discernible wall.

nodes.name: thin
nodes.definition: A discernible but hairline wall.

nodes.name: thickened
nodes.definition: A wall of measurable thickness.

nodes.name: enhancing
nodes.definition: A wall demonstrating contrast uptake.

nodes.name: nodal architecture
nodes.definition: The internal organisation of a lymph node as seen on imaging.

nodes.name: preserved fatty hilum
nodes.definition: A central fatty hilum is retained.

nodes.name: effaced fatty hilum
nodes.definition: The central fatty hilum is lost.

nodes.name: cortical thickening
nodes.definition: The cortex is thickened relative to the hilum.

nodes.name: central necrosis
nodes.definition: A non-enhancing centre within the node.

nodes.name: nodal shape
nodes.definition: The gross outline of a lymph node.

nodes.name: elongated
nodes.definition: Long axis substantially exceeds short axis.

nodes.name: rounded

nodes.name: distribution
nodes.definition: The spatial pattern of a multifocal finding across the organ or region.

nodes.name: solitary
nodes.definition: A single lesion.

nodes.name: scattered
nodes.definition: Several lesions without a discernible pattern.

nodes.name: clustered
nodes.definition: Lesions grouped in one part of the organ.

nodes.name: random
nodes.definition: Lesions distributed without respect to secondary lobular anatomy.

nodes.name: centrilobular
nodes.definition: Lesions centred on the secondary pulmonary lobule.

nodes.name: perilymphatic
nodes.definition: Lesions along lymphatic pathways.

nodes.name: miliary
nodes.definition: Innumerable uniform tiny lesions throughout.

nodes.definition: The degree of fluorodeoxyglucose uptake relative to background.

nodes.definition: Uptake not exceeding background.

nodes.name: mild
nodes.definition: Uptake mildly exceeding background.

nodes.name: moderate
nodes.definition: Uptake moderately exceeding background.

nodes.name: intense
nodes.definition: Uptake markedly exceeding background.

nodes.definition: Not present on the prior examination.

nodes.name: unchanged
nodes.definition: Without appreciable difference from the prior examination.

nodes.name: increased
nodes.definition: Larger or more numerous than on the prior examination.

nodes.name: decreased
nodes.definition: Smaller or less numerous than on the prior examination.

nodes.name: no prior available
nodes.definition: No comparable prior examination was available.

nodes.definition: Which arterial supply the infarct conforms to. A territorial infarct implicates the named artery; a watershed pattern implicates global hypoperfusion instead.

nodes.name: anterior cerebral artery
nodes.definition: Parasagittal frontal and medial parietal.

nodes.name: middle cerebral artery
nodes.definition: Lateral frontal, temporal and parietal. The commonest territory.
nodes.source_definition: The largest and most complex of the cerebral arteries. Branches of the middle cerebral artery supply the insular region, motor and premotor areas, and large regions of the association cortex. [MeSH]

nodes.name: posterior cerebral artery
nodes.definition: Occipital and medial temporal.
nodes.source_definition: Artery formed by the bifurcation of the basilar artery. Branches of the posterior cerebral artery supply portions of the occipital lobe; parietal lobe; inferior temporal gyrus, brainstem, and choroid plexus. [MeSH]

nodes.name: posterior circulation
nodes.definition: Brainstem and cerebellum, from the vertebrobasilar supply. Local: RadLex has the basilar and vertebral arteries but no concept for the territory they supply.

nodes.name: watershed
nodes.definition: Between two territories. Implies hypoperfusion rather than occlusion of one vessel.

nodes.name: non-territorial
nodes.definition: Conforming to no arterial territory. Argues against arterial infarction.

nodes.name: collection shape
nodes.definition: The outline a collection takes, which reflects the space containing it.

nodes.name: biconvex
nodes.definition: Lentiform. Bounded by sutures, where the dura is anchored.

nodes.name: crescentic
nodes.definition: Concave toward the brain. Crosses sutures but not dural reflections.

nodes.name: conforming
nodes.definition: Filling and taking the shape of the space, such as sulci and cisterns.

nodes.name: rounded
nodes.definition: Roughly spherical, as within parenchyma.

nodes.name: pneumothorax size

nodes.name: small
nodes.definition: A thin rim of pleural air.

nodes.name: moderate

nodes.name: large

nodes.definition: How old the finding is, judged from its appearance rather than from a comparison. A healed fracture on a first study has no prior to compare against and is still recognisably old.

nodes.name: acute
nodes.definition: Recent. Sharp fracture margins without callus; haemorrhage still dense.

nodes.name: subacute
nodes.definition: Intermediate. Between the acute and chronic appearances.

nodes.name: healing
nodes.definition: Callus formation with fracture margins becoming indistinct.
nodes.source_definition: Restoration of integrity to traumatized tissue. [MeSH]

nodes.name: moderate

nodes.name: large

nodes.definition: 70 to 99 percent, NASCET, and not near-occlusion.

nodes.name: near-occlusion
nodes.definition: The distal lumen is collapsed rather than merely narrowed, so a percentage understates it. Read from the string sign rather than from a ratio, which is why it is a band and never a number.

nodes.name: occluded
nodes.definition: No flow through the segment.

nodes.name: occlusiveness
nodes.definition: Whether intraluminal content obstructs flow through the lumen.

nodes.name: non-occlusive
nodes.definition: Flow persists around the content.

nodes.name: partially occlusive
nodes.definition: Flow reduced but present.

nodes.name: occlusive
nodes.definition: No flow through the segment.

nodes.name: device integrity
nodes.definition: Whether a device is intact and functioning as placed.

nodes.name: intact
nodes.definition: No abnormality of the device itself.

nodes.name: fractured
nodes.definition: The device is broken.

nodes.name: migrated
nodes.definition: The device has moved from its placed position.

nodes.name: kinked
nodes.definition: The device is acutely angulated.

nodes.name: disconnected
nodes.definition: A junction has separated.

nodes.name: tip position status
nodes.definition: Whether a device tip lies where it is intended to lie. The intended position itself is a property of the device class, not of this element.

nodes.name: appropriate
nodes.definition: At the intended site.

nodes.name: suboptimal
nodes.definition: Away from the intended site but functional.

nodes.name: malpositioned
nodes.definition: In a position that is wrong or unsafe.

nodes.name: fracture displacement
nodes.definition: Whether fracture fragments have moved out of alignment.

nodes.name: non-displaced
nodes.definition: Fragments in anatomic alignment.

nodes.name: minimally displaced
nodes.definition: Slight loss of alignment.

nodes.name: displaced
nodes.definition: Clear loss of alignment.

nodes.name: comminution
nodes.definition: Whether a fracture has more than two fragments.

nodes.name: simple
nodes.definition: Two fragments.

nodes.name: comminuted
nodes.definition: More than two fragments.

nodes.name: laterality
nodes.definition: Which side of a paired structure the finding involves.

nodes.name: left
nodes.definition: The patient's left.

nodes.name: right
nodes.definition: The patient's right.

nodes.name: bilateral
nodes.definition: Both sides.

nodes.name: midline
nodes.definition: Neither side; on the midline.

nodes.name: long-axis diameter
nodes.definition: The greatest diameter of the lesion on the plane showing its maximal dimension.
nodes.method: Greatest diameter on a single plane, measured on the sequence or window in which the lesion is best seen.

nodes.name: short-axis diameter
nodes.definition: The greatest diameter perpendicular to the long axis, on the same plane.
nodes.method: Perpendicular to the long axis on the plane of maximal dimension.

nodes.name: mean diameter
nodes.definition: The mean of the long- and short-axis diameters on the plane showing the maximal dimension.
nodes.method: Mean of long and short axis on a single plane; lung windows; Fleischner 2017 convention.

nodes.name: solid component diameter
nodes.definition: The greatest diameter of the solid component of a part-solid nodule.
nodes.method: Greatest diameter of the solid component, lung windows.

nodes.name: attenuation (Hounsfield units)
nodes.definition: The mean CT attenuation of the lesion measured within a region of interest.
nodes.method: Mean value within a region of interest covering at least two thirds of the lesion, on unenhanced images.

nodes.name: lesion count
nodes.definition: The number of discrete lesions of this class identified.
nodes.method: Count of discrete lesions; 'innumerable' is recorded as unbounded rather than as a number.

nodes.name: wall thickness
nodes.definition: The greatest thickness of the wall bounding a fluid-filled or cavitated structure.
nodes.method: Greatest thickness measured perpendicular to the wall.

nodes.name: volume
nodes.definition: The three-dimensional extent of a lesion or collection.
nodes.method: Segmented volume, or the ellipsoid approximation where stated.

nodes.name: NASCET percent stenosis
nodes.definition: Percentage reduction of the internal carotid lumen, by the NASCET method.
nodes.method: Residual lumen at the stenosis divided by the diameter of the normal distal internal carotid artery, beyond the bulb. The denominator is the landmark that makes this method carotid-specific.

nodes.name: ECST percent stenosis
nodes.definition: Percentage reduction of the internal carotid lumen, by the ECST method.
nodes.method: Residual lumen at the stenosis divided by the estimated original lumen at the same level.

nodes.name: peak systolic velocity
nodes.definition: The highest flow velocity reached during systole in the segment.
nodes.method: Angle-corrected spectral Doppler at the point of maximal narrowing, insonation angle 60 degrees or less.

nodes.name: end diastolic velocity
nodes.definition: Flow velocity at end diastole in the segment.
nodes.method: Angle-corrected spectral Doppler at the same point as the peak systolic velocity.

nodes.name: residual lumen diameter
nodes.definition: The narrowest internal diameter remaining at a stenosis.
nodes.method: Narrowest inner-to-inner diameter on the plane of maximal narrowing.

nodes.name: displacement distance
nodes.definition: How far a structure lies from its expected position.
nodes.method: Perpendicular distance from the expected midline or reference plane.

nodes.name: renal length
nodes.definition: The greatest pole-to-pole dimension of the kidney.
nodes.method: Greatest pole-to-pole length on the plane of maximal dimension.

nodes.name: involved length
nodes.definition: The length of a tubular structure affected by a process.
nodes.method: Along the long axis of the structure.

nodes.name: BI-RADS assessment
nodes.source_definition: Breast Imaging Reporting & Data System by American College of Radiology (ACR)

nodes.name: stated
nodes.definition: The source names an anatomic location and it was resolved to a node.

nodes.name: not stated
nodes.definition: The source names no anatomic location. A fact about the report. Produces an UnresolvedMention, not a finding.

nodes.name: indeterminate
nodes.definition: The source refers to a location that cannot be resolved to a single node.

nodes.name: unresolved
nodes.definition: The source names a location that extraction did not resolve. A fact about the pipeline and a defect rather than a finding. Produces an UnresolvedMention.

nodes.name: infectious
nodes.definition: Caused by an infecting organism.

nodes.name: neoplastic
nodes.definition: Caused by a neoplasm.

nodes.name: inflammatory
nodes.definition: Caused by a non-infectious inflammatory process.

nodes.name: traumatic
nodes.definition: Caused by physical injury.

nodes.name: vascular
nodes.definition: Caused by disturbance of blood supply or drainage.

nodes.name: congenital
nodes.definition: Present from birth.

nodes.name: iatrogenic
nodes.definition: Caused by medical intervention.

nodes.name: degenerative
nodes.definition: Caused by wear or ageing.

nodes.name: metabolic
nodes.definition: Caused by a metabolic derangement.

nodes.name: idiopathic
nodes.definition: No cause established.

nodes.definition: Fluoroscopy

nodes.name: MR
nodes.definition: Magnetic Resonance Imaging
nodes.source_definition: Non-invasive method of demonstrating internal anatomy based on the principle that atomic nuclei in a strong magnetic field absorb pulses of radiofrequency energy and emit them as radiowaves which can be reconstructed into computerized images. The concept includes proton spin tomographic techniques.

nodes.name: NM
nodes.definition: Nuclear Medicine

nodes.definition: Positron Emission Tomography
nodes.source_definition: An imaging technique using compounds labelled with short-lived positron-emitting radionuclides (such as carbon-11, nitrogen-13, oxygen-15 and fluorine-18) to measure cell metabolism. nodes.name: US
nodes.definition: Ultrasound
nodes.source_definition: The visualization of deep structures of the body by recording the reflections of echoes of pulses of ultrasonic waves directed into the tissues. Use of ultrasound for imaging or diagnostic purposes employs frequencies ranging from 1.6 to 10 megahertz. [MeSH]

nodes.name: XR
nodes.definition: Projection Radiography
nodes.source_definition: Examination of any part of the body for diagnostic purposes by means of roentgen rays, recording the image on a sensitized surface (such as photographic film). [MeSH]

nodes.name: pulmonary nodule
nodes.definition: A nodule within the lung parenchyma.
nodes.criterion: Distinguished from pulmonary mass at 30 mm greatest dimension (Fleischner Society, chest). Organ- and modality-specific; does not generalise.

nodes.name: solid pulmonary nodule
nodes.definition: A pulmonary nodule that completely obscures the underlying lung parenchyma.

nodes.name: part-solid pulmonary nodule
nodes.definition: A pulmonary nodule containing both a solid and a ground-glass component.

nodes.name: non-solid pulmonary nodule
nodes.definition: A pulmonary nodule that does not obscure the underlying lung parenchyma.

nodes.name: solid component of part-solid pulmonary nodule
nodes.definition: The solid portion of a part-solid pulmonary nodule.

bindings.source_label: solid component of part-solid pulmonary nodule

nodes.name: thyroid nodule
nodes.definition: A nodule within the thyroid gland.

nodes.name: adrenal nodule
nodes.definition: A nodule within the adrenal gland.

nodes.name: pulmonary mass
nodes.definition: A space-occupying lesion of the lung exceeding 30 mm.

nodes.name: hepatic mass
nodes.definition: A space-occupying lesion of the liver.

nodes.name: renal mass
nodes.definition: A space-occupying lesion of the kidney.
nodes.concept_source: ‘CT Kidney and Abdominal Renal Mass’ report template

nodes.name: renal lesion
nodes.definition: A focal abnormality of the renal parenchyma, not further characterised.

nodes.name: renal cyst
nodes.definition: A fluid-filled structure bounded by a wall, within the kidney.

nodes.name: simple renal cyst
nodes.definition: A renal cyst with uniformly fluid contents.

nodes.name: complex renal cyst
nodes.definition: A renal cyst whose contents are not uniformly fluid.

nodes.name: mural nodule
nodes.definition: A solid nodular projection from the wall of a fluid-filled structure.

nodes.name: pleural effusion
nodes.definition: Fluid within the pleural space beyond the physiologic few millilitres.

nodes.name: pneumothorax
nodes.definition: Gas within the pleural space.
nodes.source_definition:
An accumulation of air or gas in the pleural space, which may occur spontaneously or as a result of trauma or a pathological process, or be introduced deliberately ( = pneumothorax, artificial). (Dorland, 27th ed) [MeSH]
Pathophysiology.—Pneumothorax refers to the presence of gas in the pleural spac

nodes.name: intracranial hemorrhage
nodes.definition: Blood within the cranial cavity. The compartment it occupies is the clinically decisive fact and is carried by the subtypes.

nodes.name: epidural hematoma
nodes.definition: Blood in the potential space between the skull and the dura, characteristically biconvex and not crossing sutures.

nodes.name: subdural hematoma
nodes.definition: Blood in the space between the dura and the arachnoid, characteristically crescentic and crossing sutures.

nodes.name: subarachnoid hemorrhage
nodes.definition: Blood in the subarachnoid space, filling sulci and basal cisterns.

nodes.name: intraventricular hemorrhage
nodes.definition: Blood within the ventricular system.

nodes.name: intraparenchymal hemorrhage
nodes.definition: Blood within the brain parenchyma itself.

nodes.name: consolidation
nodes.definition: Replacement of alveolar air by fluid, cells or other material, obscuring the underlying vessels.
nodes.source_definition: Consolidation refers to an exudate or other product of disease that replaces alveolar air, rendering the lung solid (as in infective pneumonia). Radiographs and CT scans.—[Fleischner Society]

nodes.name: ground-glass opacity
nodes.definition: Hazy increased lung attenuation that does not obscure the vessels.
nodes.source_definition: Radiographs and CT scans.—On chest radiographs, ground-glass opacity appears as an area of hazy increased lung opacity, usually extensive, within which margins of pulmonary vessels may be indistinct. On CT scans, it appears as hazy increased opacity of lung, with preservation of bronchial and vascul

nodes.name: striated nephrogram
nodes.definition: Alternating linear bands of higher and lower attenuation radiating from the papilla to the cortex on contrast-enhanced imaging.

nodes.name: perinephric fat stranding
nodes.definition: Increased attenuation with linear or hazy strands in the perirenal fat.

nodes.name: white matter hyperintensity
nodes.definition: Increased T2 signal in the cerebral white matter.

nodes.name: acute infarct
nodes.definition: Recent ischaemic tissue death, with restricted diffusion and loss of grey-white differentiation.

nodes.name: atelectasis
nodes.definition: Incomplete expansion or collapse of lung tissue.
nodes.source_definition: Pathophysiology.—Atelectasis is reduced inflation of all or part of the lung (20). One of the commonest mechanisms is resorption of air distal to airway obstruction (eg, an endobronchial neoplasm) (21). The synonym collapse is often used interchangeably with atelectasis, particularly when it is seve

nodes.name: cerebral atrophy
nodes.definition: Loss of brain parenchymal volume beyond that expected for age.

nodes.name: encephalomalacia
nodes.definition: Established parenchymal loss with cystic change, the sequela of prior injury or infarction.

nodes.name: renal enlargement
nodes.definition: Renal length beyond the expected range for age and body size.

nodes.name: renal cortical scarring
nodes.definition: Focal cortical thinning with retraction of the overlying contour.

nodes.name: mediastinal lymphadenopathy
nodes.definition: Enlargement of one or more mediastinal lymph nodes.
nodes.source_definition:
Diseases of lymph or lymph vessels. [MeSH]
Pathology.—By common usage, the term lymphadenopathy is usually restricted to enlargement, due to any cause, of the lymph nodes. Synonyms include lymph node enlargement (preferred) and adenopathy.
CT scans.—There is a wide range in the size of normal lymph

nodes.name: external carotid artery stenosis
nodes.definition: Narrowing of the external carotid artery lumen.

nodes.name: internal carotid artery stenosis
nodes.definition: Narrowing of the internal carotid artery lumen.

nodes.name: hydronephrosis
nodes.definition: Dilation of the renal collecting system.
nodes.source_definition: Hydronephrosis is distention (dilation) of the kidney with urine, caused by backward pressure on the kidney when the flow of urine is obstructed.

nodes.name: pulmonary artery filling defect
nodes.definition: Intraluminal material within a pulmonary artery on contrast-enhanced CT.

nodes.name: rib fracture
nodes.definition: A break in the cortex of a rib.

nodes.name: midline shift
nodes.definition: Displacement of midline intracranial structures from the midline.

nodes.name: mediastinal shift
nodes.definition: Displacement of the mediastinum from the midline.

nodes.name: ventricular shunt catheter
nodes.definition: A catheter placed to divert cerebrospinal fluid from the ventricular system.
nodes.criterion: Intended tip position is the frontal horn of a lateral ventricle. The criterion sits here because it varies per device; the element carries only the verdict.

nodes.name: azygos fissure
nodes.definition: An accessory fissure formed by the azygos vein invaginating the right upper lobe during development.

nodes.name: tendon lesion
nodes.definition: A lesion involving a tendon.

nodes.name: pulmonary hamartoma
nodes.definition: A benign lung neoplasm of disorganised mesenchymal tissue, characteristically containing fat and chondroid calcification.
nodes.source_definition: A focal malformation resembling a neoplasm, composed of an overgrowth of mature cells and tissues that normally occur in the affected area. [MeSH]

nodes.name: pulmonary granuloma
nodes.definition: A focus of granulomatous inflammation in the lung, usually the sequela of prior granulomatous infection.
nodes.source_definition: A relatively small nodular inflammatory lesion containing grouped mononuclear phagocytes, caused by infectious and noninfectious agents. [MeSH]

nodes.name: intrapulmonary lymph node
nodes.definition: A normal lymph node within the lung parenchyma, characteristically perifissural, oval and subpleural.

nodes.name: lung cancer
nodes.definition: Primary malignant neoplasm arising from lung tissue.

nodes.name: empyema
nodes.definition: Infected pleural fluid: pus in the pleural space.
nodes.source_definition: Presence of pus in a hollow organ or body cavity. [MeSH]

nodes.name: hemothorax
nodes.definition: Blood in the pleural space.

nodes.name: chylothorax
nodes.definition: Chyle in the pleural space from disruption or obstruction of the thoracic duct.

nodes.name: parapneumonic effusion
nodes.definition: Pleural effusion accompanying pneumonia, before it becomes an empyema.

bindings.source_label: Pleural effusion associated with pulmonary infection

nodes.name: tension pneumothorax
nodes.definition: A pneumothorax under positive pressure, displacing the mediastinum and impairing venous return. A physiological state concluded from imaging signs together with the clinical picture, not a feature seen directly.
nodes.source_definition: Pathophysiology.—Pneumothorax refers to the presence of gas in the pleural space. Qualifiers include spontaneous, traumatic, diagnostic, and tension. nodes.name: heart failure
nodes.definition: Inability of the heart to maintain adequate output, with venous congestion.

nodes.name: pneumonia
nodes.definition: Infection of the lung parenchyma.
nodes.source_definition:
Inflammation of the lungs. [MeSH]

nodes.name: pulmonary edema
nodes.definition: Accumulation of fluid in the lung, most often from raised left atrial pressure.

nodes.name: malignant neoplastic disease
nodes.definition: Any malignant neoplasm, primary or metastatic.

nodes.name: malignant pleural effusion
nodes.definition: Pleural effusion from involvement of the pleura by malignancy.

nodes.name: nephrotic syndrome
nodes.definition: Heavy proteinuria with hypoalbuminemia and edema.

nodes.name: pulmonary embolism
nodes.definition: Thromboembolic occlusion of pulmonary arteries.
nodes.source_definition: Embolism in the pulmonary artery or one of its branches. [MeSH]

nodes.name: acute pyelonephritis
nodes.definition: Active bacterial infection of the renal parenchyma and collecting system.

nodes.name: chronic pyelonephritis
nodes.definition: Pyelonephritis with established parenchymal damage from prior or recurrent infection.

nodes.name: renal cell carcinoma
nodes.definition: A primary malignant neoplasm arising from renal tubular epithelium.
nodes.source_definition: A heterogeneous group of sporadic or hereditary carcinoma derived from cells of the kidneys. There are several subtypes including the clear cells, the papillary, the chromophobe, the collecting duct, the spindle cells (sarcomatoid), or mixed cell-type carcinoma. [MeSH]

nodes.name: hepatocellular carcinoma
nodes.definition: A primary malignant neoplasm arising from hepatocytes.
nodes.source_definition: A primary malignant neoplasm of epithelial liver cells. It ranges from a well-differentiated tumor with epithelial cells indistinguishable from normal hepatocytes to a poorly differentiated neoplasm. The cells may be uniform or markedly pleomorphic, or form giant cells. Several classification scheme

nodes.name: adrenal adenoma
nodes.definition: A benign neoplasm of the adrenal cortex.
nodes.source_definition: A benign epithelial tumor with a glandular organization. [MeSH]

nodes.name: metastatic disease
nodes.definition: Neoplasm that has spread from a primary site to a discontiguous site.
nodes.source_definition: The transfer of a neoplasm from one organ or part of the body to another remote from the primary site. [MeSH]

nodes.name: reactive lymphadenopathy
nodes.definition: Lymph node enlargement secondary to a benign immune response.

nodes.name: cerebral infarction
nodes.definition: Tissue death in the brain from interruption of arterial supply.
nodes.source_definition:
Formation of an infarct, which is necrosis in tissue due to local ischemia resulting from obstruction of blood circulation, most commonly by a thrombus or embolus. [MeSH]

nodes.name: chronic small vessel disease
nodes.definition: Chronic ischaemic change of the cerebral small vessels.
